# CLI reference

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/reference/cli-reference

_Look up the flags, subcommands, environment variables and exit codes of the three Zilkworm tools._

# CLI reference

Use this page to look up a flag, subcommand, environment variable or exit code for any of Zilkworm's three command-line tools. Everything here matches `v0.1.0-alpha.7`.

`z6m_prover` drives the SP1 Hypercube guest and `z6m_prover_airbender` drives the Airbender guest. The third tool, `state_transition`, runs a block natively, outside any zkVM.

## z6m_prover (Hypercube)

The release ships this binary as `z6m_prover_hypercube`, and `make z6m_prover` builds it at `prover/target/release/z6m_prover`. You can run it in three forms:

```bash
z6m_prover --service [flags]         # fetch, execute and prove in a loop
z6m_prover --test-service [flags]    # execute downloaded blocks or EEST fixtures offline
z6m_prover <subcommand> [flags]      # fetch, execute, prove, setup or verify once
```

Given no mode and no subcommand, it exits with an error. At startup it loads a `.env` file from the working directory.

### Top-level flags

| Flag | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `--service` | off | Run the service loop. Needs `--rpc-url`. |
| `--test-service` | off | Execute on the CPU, with no RPC and no proving. With `--test-dir` it runs EEST fixtures. Otherwise it runs bundles from `--data-dir` between `--start-block` and `--end-block`. Conflicts with `--service` and with any subcommand. |
| `--rpc-url` | none | JSON-RPC endpoint. It must serve `debug_getRawBlock` and `debug_executionWitness`. |
| `--data-dir` | `temp` | Root data directory. Blocks go to `<data-dir>/blocks/<N>/`, logs to the root. |
| `--save-all-responses` | off | Also save the raw RPC JSON next to each bundle. In service mode it also fetches blocks that match no interval. |
| `--download-only` | off | Service mode: fetch bundles only. It overrides `--prove-every` and `--execute-every`. |
| `--prove-every` | unset | Service mode: prove blocks whose number is a multiple of N. 0 or unset means never. |
| `--execute-every` | unset | Execute blocks whose number is a multiple of N, unless they are proved. `--test-service` without `--test-dir` defaults it to 1 and rejects 0. |
| `--post-every` | unset | Unused. |
| `--start-block` | chain head + 1 | First block. `--test-service` needs it unless `--test-dir` is set. |
| `--end-block` | follow the head | Last block, inclusive. The service exits after it. |
| `--execution-log-file` | `executionLogs.log` in the data or test directory | Read by `--test-service` only. The service and `execute` always append to `<data-dir>/executionLogs.log`. |
| `--test-dir` | none | EEST fixtures for `--test-service`, scanned recursively for `.mfbd` and `.json` files. |
| `--max-file-size` | `20971520` | `--test-service --test-dir` skips larger files. 0 means no limit. |
| `--pk-path` | `pk.bin` | Unused. The proving key is generated in-process. |
| `--proof-type` | `compressed` | Service-mode proof mode: `core`, `compressed`, `groth16` or `plonk`. Unknown values fall back to `compressed`. |
| `--ethproofs-endpoint`, `--ethproofs-token`, `--ethproofs-cluster-id` | none | Ethproofs reporting in `--service`. Set all three, or reporting stays off without a warning. |

### Subcommands

| Subcommand | Options | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `fetch` | `--rpc-url`, `--block-number`, `--data-dir`, `--save-all-responses`, `--geth` | Fetch one block and its witness and write `<data-dir>/blocks/<N>/flatWitnessBundle<N>.mfbd`. An unset or 0 block number means the chain head. A bundle already on disk is reused. |
| `execute` | `--block-number`, `--file-name`, `--is-test`, `--data-dir` | Run the guest on the CPU executor without proving. |
| `prove` | as `execute`, plus `--pk-path`, `--proof-path`, `--proof-type` | Prove one block. The three extra options are unused. See the limits below. |
| `setup` | `--pk-path`, `--vk-path` | No-op. Nothing is written. |
| `verify` | `--proof-path`, `--vk-path` | No-op. No verification runs. |

By default, `execute` and `prove` read `<data-dir>/blocks/<N>/flatWitnessBundle<N>.mfbd`. With `--is-test` they read `ethTests<N>.json` as an EEST fixture instead, and `--file-name` overrides the block-number lookup.

When `execute` finishes, it prints `Executed block <N> (gas_used=..., cycles=..., prover_gas=..., syscall_count=...)` and appends a line to `<data-dir>/executionLogs.log`. It exits 1 when `gas_used` is 0.

`--geth` exists only on `fetch`; the service always reads the reth and alloy witness shape.

Before you reach for `prove`, know its limits as of `v0.1.0-alpha.7`:

- It always uses the CUDA prover in compressed mode, and ignores `SP1_PROVER` and `--proof-type`.
- It discards the proof. Nothing is written to disk, and the summary line prints `gas_used=0` and an empty path.
- A key setup failure prints `ERROR` but still exits 0, and a proving failure is not reported at all.
- It never posts to Ethproofs.

If you need proof files, use `--service`.

### Environment variables

- `SP1_PROVER` selects the service-mode backend. Only `cuda` is special-cased, as the local GPU prover; any other value, or none, gives you the CPU prover. `execute` always uses the CPU, and `prove` always uses CUDA.
- `NETWORK_PRIVATE_KEY` appears in `.env.example` for the Succinct Prover Network, but nothing reads it, because `network` and `mock` modes are not wired up.
- `RUST_LOG` sets the log filter, which defaults to `warn`.

For Ethproofs, pass the flags. This binary reads no `ETHPROOFS_*` variables.

## z6m_prover_airbender

`make z6m_prover_airbender` builds this one at `prover/prover_airbender/target/release/z6m_prover_airbender`, and the image `ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-airbender` ships it together with the guest. Like the Hypercube host, it runs as `--service`, as `--test-service`, or with one subcommand.

### Top-level flags

| Flag | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `--service` | off | Run the proving service. Needs `--rpc-url`. Conflicts with subcommands. |
| `--test-service` | off | Execute downloaded blocks from `--start-block` to `--end-block` on the simulator. Needs both. Conflicts with subcommands. |
| `--data-dir` | `temp` | Root directory with a `blocks/` subdirectory. |
| `--start-block`, `--end-block` | unset | Block range. |
| `--execution-log-file` | `<data-dir>/executionLogs.log` | Read by `--test-service` only. |
| `--guest-bin` | `prover/guest_airbender/build/z6m_guest` | Guest path without the `.bin` or `.text` extension. The default needs the repo root as working directory. |
| `--cycles` | `5000000000` | Simulator cycle bound. Proving clamps it to `1073741822`. |
| `--replay-threads` | unset, 8 on the GPU backend | CPU threads that replay the trace while proving. Env `Z6M_REPLAY_THREADS`. Also accepted after a subcommand. |
| `--rpc-url` | none | JSON-RPC endpoint. Required for `--service`. |
| `--ws-url` | none | WebSocket endpoint for `newHeads`. Without it the service polls `--rpc-url`. |
| `--gpu` | off | Prove on the GPU in service mode. Required with `--prove-every`. |
| `--prove-every` | unset | Service mode: prove blocks whose number is a multiple of N. |
| `--execute-every` | unset | Service mode: execute without proving every N-th block. |
| `--post-every` | unset | Accepted and never read. |
| `--output-dir` | `proofs` | Service proofs go to `<output-dir>/<N>/proof.bin`. |
| `--save-all-responses` | off | Save the raw RPC responses. |
| `--fetch-timeout` | `60` | Seconds one fetch attempt may take. Minimum 1. |
| `--max-lag` | `10` | Blocks the service may fall behind the tip before it skips ahead. 0 never skips. |
| `--ethproofs-endpoint`, `--ethproofs-token`, `--ethproofs-cluster-id` | none | Ethproofs reporting. Env `ETHPROOFS_ENDPOINT`, `ETHPROOFS_TOKEN`, `ETHPROOFS_CLUSTER_ID`. Set all three or nothing is posted. |

### Subcommands

| Subcommand | Options | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `execute` | `--block-number`, `--file-name`, `--data-dir`, `--is-test`, `--flamegraph <svg>` | Run the guest on the simulator. Check the committed block hash against the input. Fail if the guest does not finish successfully. |
| `vk` | `--output`, default `vk.bin` | Compute the guest's EVKEY001 v2 verification key from the guest and the `FSV_DIR` programs. |
| `prove` | `--block-number`, `--file-name`, `--data-dir`, `--is-test`, `--backend gpu` or `cpu`, `--output-dir` | Run a simulator preflight, prove to the final recursion layer, check the output and write `<output-dir>/proof.bin`. Defaults: `gpu`, `proofs`. |
| `bench` | `--file-name` (required), `--iterations` (default 5), `--backend` | Prove one MFBD file repeatedly with one prover. Print each time and the min, median and max. |
| `verify` | `--proof`, `--vk`, and `--file-name` or `--block-hash` | Verify the proof against the key. Check that its output is the hash of the input's last valid block, or the given hash. |

Without `--file-name`, input comes from `<data-dir>/blocks/<N>/flatWitnessBundle<N>.mfbd`, and if that file is missing the prover tries the legacy `unifiedBlockAndStateRlp<N>.bin`. With `--is-test` the input is an EEST JSON fixture. Proof files are gzip EPROOF01 v2. The `cpu` backend is slow, and [Airbender prover](../provers/airbender-prover.md) gives its memory need.

Both `execute` and `--test-service` append to the execution log, and `execute` warns you when a run has more cycles than the prover takes.

### Environment variables

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `Z6M_REPLAY_THREADS` | Same as `--replay-threads`. |
| `FSV_DIR` | Directory of the `fsv_*` recursion verifier programs. Unset, the prover uses `tools/gkr_verifier` of the zksync-airbender checkout it was built from. The image sets it. |
| `RISCV_MERGE_WINDOW` | Leave unset. The binary sets it to 0, and any other value is an error. The prover's JIT would otherwise fuse word stores the guest jumps into, and prove a wrong run. |
| `Z6M_CONCURRENT_PREFLIGHT` | When set, the service simulates each block alongside proving instead of first. A block the guest rejects then stops the service. |
| `RECURSION_UNROLLED_BLAKE`, `RECURSION_BRIDGE_BLAKE`, `RECURSION_FINAL_BLAKE`, `RECURSION_UNIFIED_BLAKE` | Leave unset. Other values make proofs no published key accepts, so `prove` and `bench` refuse to start. |
| `ETHPROOFS_ENDPOINT`, `ETHPROOFS_TOKEN`, `ETHPROOFS_CLUSTER_ID` | Same as the Ethproofs flags. |
| `RUST_LOG` | Log filter. Defaults to `info`. |

### Docker entrypoint

The image's entrypoint runs the prover with any arguments you pass, plus `--guest-bin`. If you pass none, it runs the service from the environment variables below. It first computes the verification key into `$DATA_DIR/vk-<rev>-<id>/vk.bin`, then runs `--service --gpu` and restarts the service whenever it exits. Proofs go to `$DATA_DIR/proofs/<N>/proof.bin`.

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `RPC_URL` | required | JSON-RPC endpoint that serves `debug_executionWitness`. |
| `WS_URL` | none | WebSocket endpoint for `newHeads`. Without it the service polls. |
| `PROVE_EVERY` | `100` | Prove blocks whose number is a multiple of this. |
| `EXECUTE_EVERY` | none | Execute without proving every N-th block. |
| `START_BLOCK` | chain tip | First block. A restart drops it and starts at the tip. |
| `FETCH_TIMEOUT` | `60` | Seconds one fetch attempt may take. |
| `MAX_LAG` | `10` | Blocks behind the tip before the service skips ahead. 0 never skips. |
| `DATA_DIR` | `/data` | Key, blocks, logs and proofs. Mount a volume here. |
| `ETHPROOFS_ENDPOINT`, `ETHPROOFS_TOKEN`, `ETHPROOFS_CLUSTER_ID` | none | Post to Ethproofs. With any one unset the run is a dry run. |
| `RESTART_DELAY` | `30` | Seconds to wait before a restart. |
| `PROVER_EXTRA_ARGS` | none | More prover options, split on spaces. |

## state_transition

`state_transition` runs the whole state transition natively. You get it from a release as `state_transition_linux_x86_64`, or from a local build at `build/zilk_core/dev/cli/state_transition`.

```bash
state_transition <flatWitnessBundle.mfbd>|<test.json>|<test_dir>
```

The tool picks its mode from the path. A path ending in `.json` runs as an EEST blockchain test, any other file runs as an MFBD bundle, and a directory is scanned recursively. For a bundle it prints `Cumulative Gas Used: <n>`, `FAIL: <path>` or `SKIP: <path>`.

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Passed. For a directory: at least one file passed and none failed. |
| 1 | Failed, or no argument given. For a directory: any file failed. |
| 2 | Skipped. For a directory: nothing passed. |
| 3 | The bundle could not be read, or an exception was thrown. |
| 4 | An unknown exception. |

Watch out for directory mode. It only picks up `.json` and `.bin` files, so a directory of `.mfbd` files runs nothing and exits 2; pass bundles one at a time instead.

## Further reading

- [Hypercube prover](../provers/hypercube-prover.md)
- [Airbender prover](../provers/airbender-prover.md)
- [Ethproofs posting](../provers/ethproofs-posting.md)
- [`prover/prover_airbender/README.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/prover/prover_airbender/README.md)
- [`docs/airbender-docker-service.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/airbender-docker-service.md)

# Releases and assets

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/reference/releases-and-assets

_Each Zilkworm release ships host binaries, guest images and verification keys, listed here with its measured results._

# Releases and assets

This page tells you what each Zilkworm release ships, which verification key goes with which guest, and how a release is cut.

Releases are on the [GitHub releases page](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/releases), and so far all of them are pre-releases. Each release body opens with the matching section of `CHANGELOG.md`.

This is the only page on the site with performance numbers. Each one comes from the CHANGELOG section of the tag on its line.

## Current status

The latest release is `v0.1.0-alpha.7`, published 25 October 2026, and the EEST pin is `tests@v21.0.1`. Airbender is live on Ethproofs, and the `v0.1.0-alpha.5` result below has Ethproofs provenance. There is no Hypercube cluster on Ethproofs.

The overview's status strip reads `src/data/status.json` in the docs repository, so update that file and this page together on each release.

## Release history

| Tag | Title | Highlights |
|---|---|---|
| `v0.1.0-alpha.1` | First Public Alpha | The C++ guest runs on SP1 Hypercube, with precompiles on SP1 syscalls. |
| `v0.1.0-alpha.2` | More performance more testing and more stability | The notes report "Close to 10% improved proving time", and the EEST suite runs inside the Hypercube prover. |
| `v0.1.0-alpha.2-ere` | ERE zkEVM benchmark integration | This is alpha.2 plus the ERE benchmark integration, and it has no CHANGELOG section. |
| `v0.1.0-alpha.3` | MFBD witness format, pre-trie validation and Amsterdam | It adds the MFBD bundle and pre-state checks against the parent root. |
| `v0.1.0-alpha.4` | ERE stateless input, stateless new-payload checks and Sepolia | On tests-zkevm v21.0.1, 33,635 of 33,637 fixtures report `output_matched`. On Sepolia, the estimated prover cost is 0.500x Reth 0.1.0-rc.4's. |
| `v0.1.0-alpha.5` | Real-time proving with Airbender v3 | Airbender proves 200 consecutive mainnet blocks at a 3.4 s median on 2x RTX 5090, with the slowest at 6.1 s. That run has Ethproofs provenance from 15 October 2026. On 4x RTX 5090 the median is 2.58 s. |
| `v0.1.0-alpha.6` | Native statelessInputBytes with the HashState backend | In the CI 200-block benchmark, Hypercube guest cycles fall from 23.21B at alpha.5 to 17.44B (-24.9%), and Airbender's from 27.86B to 27.65B (-0.8%). The HashState ERE guest is at Z/R 0.477 against Reth 0.1.0-rc.4. |
| `v0.1.0-alpha.7` | SP1 v6.9.0 and a leaner HashState guest | The ERE estimated cost changes by −1.70% on Sepolia 11982400..11982499, and the SP1 bump leaves guest cycles as they were on alpha.6. |

## Assets in v0.1.0-alpha.7

| Asset | What it is | zkVM | Input |
|---|---|---|---|
| `z6m_prover_hypercube` | The Hypercube host `z6m_prover` for x86_64 Linux, with the MFBD guest embedded | SP1 Hypercube v6.9.0 | `.mfbd`, or EEST JSON with `--is-test` |
| `z6m_guest_hypercube_mfbd.elf` | DirectState guest, rv64im, built `USE_HASH_KEY=OFF` | SP1 | MFBD, EJSN |
| `z6m_guest_hypercube_mfbd.vk` | Its SP1 verifying key, from `derive_vk` | SP1 | none |
| `stateless-validator-zilkworm-sp1-v6.9.0.elf` | HashState guest, rv64im; the ERE guest | SP1 v6.9.0 | Raw `statelessInputBytes`, EJSN |
| `stateless-validator-zilkworm-sp1-v6.9.0.vk` | Its SP1 verifying key, named as the ere-guests handbook asks | SP1 | none |
| `state_transition_linux_x86_64` | Native runner, DirectState | none | `.mfbd`, `.json` or a directory |
| `z6m_guest_airbender.bin` | rv32 guest image, copied out of the release image, built `USE_HASH_KEY=ON` | Airbender v3 | MFBD, EJSN |
| `z6m_guest_airbender.text` | Text section of the same guest | Airbender v3 | none |
| `z6m_guest_airbender.vk` | EVKEY001 v2 verification key, computed on CPU by the image's prover | Airbender v3 | none |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | sha256 of every file above | none | none |

The release also tags the image `ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-airbender:<tag>`, and its notes give the image digest and the sha256 of `z6m_guest_airbender.vk`. If you run an Ethproofs cluster, upload that key to it so its proofs show as verified.

## Verification keys

A key belongs to one guest build. The Hypercube MFBD guest is built with `USE_HASH_KEY=OFF`, and the Airbender guest with `USE_HASH_KEY=ON`. Since the key depends on that flag, your local build reproduces a published key only if you use the same setting.

Keys can also change when the guest code does not. Keys published for `v0.1.0-alpha.6` do not verify `v0.1.0-alpha.7` proofs, and part of the reason is the SP1 bump. SP1 v6.9.0 loads a guest's initial memory correctly, where v6.6.0 zeroed up to four bytes of it ([sp1#2981](https://github.com/succinctlabs/sp1/pull/2981)). On top of that, [#141](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/pull/141) changed the MFBD and Airbender guests and their keys in `v0.1.0-alpha.7`. Always check a proof against the key from its own release.

## Older asset names

Two earlier releases used other names. `v0.1.0-alpha.5` shipped the Hypercube guest as `z6m_guest_hypercube.{elf,vk}`. The `v0.1.0-alpha.6` release notes call the ERE guest `z6m_guest_hypercube_slib`, while its assets are `stateless-validator-zilkworm-sp1-v6.6.0.{elf,vk}`.

## Release procedure

To cut a release, you work through five steps:

1. Create a branch, usually `release/X.Y.Z`.
2. Bump `PROJECT_VERSION` in `CMakeLists.txt` to `X.Y.Z`.
3. Add a `## vX.Y.Z - <title>` section to `CHANGELOG.md`. It becomes the release body.
4. Commit and push the branch.
5. Tag the release commit `vX.Y.Z` and push the tag. The tag must equal `PROJECT_VERSION`, or the workflow fails.

From there the `Release` workflow takes over. It tags the Airbender image, builds the assets, writes `SHA256SUMS.txt` and publishes the release, then ends with an ERE benchmark run on the published guest.

If you tag a commit on `main`, wait until its `Airbender Prover Image` run has finished. Otherwise the image is built twice, and its commit and release tags can name two different builds.

## Further reading

- [Choosing a prover](../provers/choosing-a-prover.md)
- [Benchmarks and CI](./benchmarks-and-ci.md)
- [ERE validation](../testing/ere-validation.md)
- [`docs/release.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/release.md)
- [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

# Building from source

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/reference/building-from-source

_Build the native tools, the guests and the host provers from source, and run the unit tests._

# Building from source

Follow this page to build Zilkworm's native tools, guests and host provers from source, and to run the unit tests.

## Native build

For the native build you need CMake 3.28 or newer, Ninja and GCC 15. Clone the repository with its one submodule, `third_party/evmone`, which holds ZVM1, the Zilkworm fork of evmone. Then configure and build:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm
cd zilkworm
git submodule update --init --recursive
cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -B build -G Ninja -S .
cmake --build build -j$(nproc)
```

To build the guests you also need the xPack `riscv-none-elf-gcc` cross-compiler. CI pins version `15.2.0-1.1`:

```bash
npm install -g xpm
xpm install @xpack-dev-tools/riscv-none-elf-gcc@15.2.0-1.1 --global
```

The Makefile puts the first xPack GCC it finds under `~/.local/xPacks` on `PATH`, or under `~/Library/xPacks` on macOS. Since it takes the first one, keep only `15.2.0-1.1` installed, or a guest can build with an older compiler.

## state_transition

The native build produces `build/zilk_core/dev/cli/state_transition`, which runs the whole state transition outside any zkVM. Point it at a bundle:

```bash
build/zilk_core/dev/cli/state_transition <flatWitnessBundle.mfbd>
```

It also takes an EEST blockchain-test JSON or a directory, and [CLI reference](./cli-reference.md#state_transition) lists its inputs and exit codes.

## Converters

Three converters sit next to it, and each one writes the MFBD bundle that [Witness formats](../inside-the-guest/witness-formats.md) describes.

- `json_witness_to_flat_bundle` reads a witness JSON document on stdin and writes the bundle to stdout.
- `legacy_to_flat_bundle <in.bin> <out.mfbd>` converts an older `unifiedBlockAndStateRlp<N>.bin` file.
- `eest_to_flat_bundle` converts EEST blockchain-test JSON. Its `emit --json <PATH> --index <N>` writes one case to stdout, and `bulk-convert --input-dir <D> --output-dir <D>` mirrors a whole tree.

## Guest targets

Each guest target cross-compiles the C++ core for one zkVM.

| Target | Builds | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `make z6m_guest` | Hypercube DirectState guest for MFBD input, `USE_HASH_KEY=OFF` | `prover/guest_hypercube/build/z6m_guest.elf` |
| `make z6m_guest_slib` | Hypercube HashState guest for `statelessInputBytes`, with `-DZ6M_HASH_STATE=ON` | `prover/guest_hypercube/build-slib/z6m_guest.elf` |
| `make z6m_guest_airbender` | Airbender guest, `USE_HASH_KEY=ON` | `prover/guest_airbender/build/z6m_guest.bin` and `.text` |
| `make z6m_guest_zisk` | ZisK guest, only on PR #86; see [ZisK prover](../provers/zisk-prover.md) | `prover/guest_zisk/build/z6m_guest.elf` |

The Hypercube guests use the toolchain file `prover/guest_hypercube/cmake/riscv64im-sp1.cmake`, and the Airbender guest uses `prover/guest_airbender/cmake/riscv32im.cmake`. Keep an eye on `USE_HASH_KEY`, because it changes the verification key, as [Releases and assets](./releases-and-assets.md#verification-keys) explains.

## Host targets

On the host side, three targets build the provers and a fourth builds `derive_vk`.

| Target | Builds | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `make z6m_prover` | The MFBD guest and the Hypercube host that embeds it | `prover/target/release/z6m_prover` |
| `make z6m_prover_slib` | The same host with the HashState guest embedded | `prover/target/release/z6m_prover` |
| `make z6m_prover_airbender` | The Airbender guest and its host | `prover/prover_airbender/target/release/z6m_prover_airbender` |
| `make derive_vk` | `derive_vk <elf> <vk>`, which writes a guest's 32-byte SP1 key | `prover/target/release/derive_vk` |

`make z6m_prover` and `make z6m_prover_slib` write the same binary, so whichever you built last wins. Both `make z6m_guest_vk` and `make ere-bin` run `derive_vk` with `SP1_PROVER=mock`.

:::caution
If your tree ran `make z6m_prover_slib` before `v0.1.0-alpha.7`, delete `prover/guest_hypercube/build/z6m_guest.elf` once. Otherwise `make z6m_prover` keeps embedding the HashState guest.
:::

The Airbender host builds with GPU support by default. If you have no CUDA, build it with `cargo build --release --no-default-features` in `prover/prover_airbender`, as CI does. Each Rust workspace pins its own toolchain in `rust-toolchain.toml`.

## Tests

To build and run the unit tests the way CI does:

```bash
cmake -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build --target zilkworm.tests
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure --parallel
```

Add `-DZ6M_HASH_STATE=ON` to run them on the HashState backend. For the EEST suites, see [Execution spec tests](../testing/execution-spec-tests.md) and [RISC-V tests under QEMU](../testing/riscv-tests-under-qemu.md).

## Code style

The C++ code follows Silkworm's style, which is the C++ Core Guidelines plus Google's C++ style guide, with project changes. The format rules live in `zilk_core/.clang-format`, and the lint checks in `zilk_core/.clang-tidy`.

## Repo docs

The Zilkworm repository has its own docs on each part:

- [`docs/architecture.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): the layers, the input envelope and the public values.
- [`docs/mfbd_design_specs.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/mfbd_design_specs.md): the MFBD spec for producers and verifiers.
- [`docs/hashstate.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/hashstate.md): the HashState backend and its SSZ input.
- [`docs/airbender_architecture.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/airbender_architecture.md): the rv32 guest, its toolchain and its CSR delegations.
- [`docs/release.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/release.md): the release process.

## Further reading

- [Execution spec tests](../testing/execution-spec-tests.md)
- [CLI reference](./cli-reference.md)
- [Benchmarks and CI](./benchmarks-and-ci.md)
- [`Makefile`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/Makefile)

# Benchmarks and CI

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/reference/benchmarks-and-ci

_Make targets benchmark the Hypercube, HashState, Airbender and ERE paths, and GitHub workflows run them._

# Benchmarks and CI

With this page you can run each benchmark yourself and find out which GitHub workflow runs what in CI. The benchmarks measure cycles and estimated prover cost, and their results for each release are on [Releases and assets](./releases-and-assets.md).

## Hypercube 200-block benchmark

`make sp1-benchmark` runs the Hypercube MFBD guest over 200 mainnet blocks. In order, it builds `z6m_prover`, runs `make sp1-benchmark-corpus` and then runs `tools/scripts/sp1_benchmark.py`.

`sp1-benchmark-corpus` converts each `temp/200_benchmark_blocks/<N>/unifiedBlockAndStateRlp<N>.bin` with `legacy_to_flat_bundle` and writes the bundles to `temp/200_benchmark_blocks_mfbd_v2/<N>/`. You can override the two paths with `BENCH_SRC_DIR` and `BENCH_CORPUS_DIR`. CI downloads the raw blocks from the [`benchmark-200-spread`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm-testdata/releases/tag/benchmark-200-spread) release of `erigontech/zilkworm-testdata`.

The script takes `--dir`, and optionally `--start` and `--count`, and writes `execution.log` and `summary.md` to `temp/benchmarks/benchmark_<timestamp>/`. It does not compare against a baseline. If you want to compare two builds, run it on each and compare the totals yourself.

## HashState benchmark

`make slib-benchmark` measures the SP1 cycles of the HashState guest. It downloads the 30M-gas `tests-zkevm-benchmark@v21.0.5` fixtures with `gh release download`, so make sure `gh` is logged in first. It then builds `z6m_prover_slib` and runs each case through `z6m_prover execute --is-test`, writing per-case results to `temp/slib_benchmark/per_case.csv`.

Read these numbers with care, because they do not measure the production path. `execute --is-test` sends the whole fixture JSON to the guest, and parsing it is about half the cycles. The ERE benchmark below measures the production input, and [`docs/slib_benchmark.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/slib_benchmark.md) has the details.

Also, `z6m_prover_slib` replaces `prover/target/release/z6m_prover`, so run `make z6m_prover` again before your next MFBD run.

## Airbender benchmark

For Airbender, `tools/scripts/airbender_benchmark.sh --dir <corpus>` runs `z6m_prover_airbender execute` on every bundle in the corpus. It expects the layout that `make sp1-benchmark-corpus` writes. It reports gas and cycle statistics and keeps its logs in `temp/airbender_benchmark/`. Use `-j`, `-s`, `-e`, `-l` and `-t` to set the jobs, block range, log directory and per-block timeout.

Don't confuse this script with the prover's `bench` subcommand, which proves one block several times.

## ERE benchmark

The ERE benchmark runs the HashState guest inside SP1 through `ere-hosts`, on each fixture's `statelessInputBytes`. `make ere-cost` estimates the guest's SP1 cost and prints a cost table. To see how that compares with Reth, `make ere-compare` runs `ere-cost`, then estimates Reth's cost on the same fixtures and compares the two. If you already have an `ere-cost` run, `make ere-compare -o ere-cost` reuses it.

Both targets run in a `zkevm-benchmark-workload` checkout at `ERE_WORKLOAD_DIR`. To run the guest from `make ere-bin`, set `ERE_BIN_PATH=build/ere-bin`; without it, the published guest is downloaded. [ERE validation](../testing/ere-validation.md) covers the setup, `ere-validate` and the `output_matched` check.

## CI workflows

Every workflow lives in [`.github/workflows/`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/tree/main/.github/workflows), and most run in the `ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-ci` image. Here is what each one runs, and when:

| File | Name | What it runs | Trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unit-tests.yml` | Unit Tests | `zilkworm.tests` three ways: Debug, HashState, and rv32 paths with ASan and UBSan | push, PR to main, master; dispatch |
| `eest-blockchain-tests.yml` | EEST Blockchain Tests | `make eest-blockchain-tests`, native on MFBD | push, PR to main, master, release/*; dispatch |
| `hypercube-eest.yml` | HyperCube EEST Blockchain Tests | `make z6m_prover`, then `eest_runner.py` over the MFBD corpus on the SP1 executor | push, PR to main, master, release/* on path changes; dispatch |
| `sp1-benchmark.yml` | Hypercube 200-block Bench | `sp1-benchmark-corpus` and `sp1_benchmark.py` | push, PR to main, master, release/*; dispatch |
| `hypercube-slib-benchmark.yml` | HyperCube slib Benchmark | `make slib-benchmark` | dispatch only |
| `airbender-eest.yml` | Airbender EEST Blockchain Tests | The guest, the host without GPU features, and `make eest` in `prover/prover_airbender` | push, PR to main, master on path changes; dispatch |
| `airbender-benchmark.yml` | Airbender 200-block Bench | `airbender_benchmark.sh` on the 200-block corpus | push, PR to main, master; dispatch |
| `airbender-image.yml` | Airbender Prover Image | Build and push `ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-airbender`; Airbender release assets | push to main on path changes, PR on path changes; dispatch; called by Release |
| `qemu-eest-blockchain.yml` | Qemu EESTs on RV32IM | `qemu_runner` targets `xpack-elf-eest` and `rerun-ctest` | push, PR to main, master, release/*; every 3 days; dispatch |
| `qemu-eest-blockchain-rv64.yml` | Qemu EESTs on RV64IM | The same with `ARCH=rv64` | push, PR to main, master, release/*; every 3 days; dispatch |
| `ere-benchmark.yml` | ERE Benchmark | `ere-bin`, `ere-validate`, `ere-cost`, and `ere-compare` when asked | push to release/*; dispatch; called by Release |
| `release.yml` | Release | Tag check, Airbender image, `make z6m_prover z6m_guest_vk ere-bin`, `state_transition`, `release-artifacts`, publish, then an ERE run without Reth | tag `v*`; dispatch |
| `ci-image.yml` | Build CI Image | Build `ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-ci` | push to main, master, release/* on Dockerfile changes; dispatch |
| `zisk-eest.yml` | ZisK EEST Blockchain Tests | PR #86 only. EEST under `ziskemu`, execute only | push, PR to main, master, release/* on path changes; dispatch |
| `zisk-benchmark.yml` | ZisK 200-block Bench | PR #86 only. The 200-block corpus under `ziskemu`, execute only | push, PR to main, master, release/* on path changes; dispatch |

The two ZisK workflows exist only on [PR #86](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/pull/86), and they run in their own image, `ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-ci-zisk`.
